title: The Ghost of the Green Zone
premise: Quentin Sandoval, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one exchange that ended in blood, receives a debt notice from a stranger claiming she owes a favor from a night she cannot remember in Baghdad's Green Zone. The 'favor' was a coerced choice made under a black-ops training program that manufactured negotiators like her, and now the network wants her to talk a whistleblower out of exposing them before Frankfurt markets open. Instead, Quentin turns her skills against her handlers, trading secrets, allies, and finally her own anonymity to burn the program down. She succeeds, but at the cost of the carefully invisible life she built, ending the book walking into daylight as a named witness rather than a ghost.
about_author: Oscar Oyelaran is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to people talk each other back from ledges. He writes thrillers about the machinery of persuasion and the people it leaves behind.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Quentin, mid-negotiation with a bank robber who reminds her of her old failure, receives an envelope: photos of herself in Baghdad, a date she can't place, and one line—'You owe us.' POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of a life built on control.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Quentin digs through sealed records and finds a redacted hostage exchange from 2011 where she was the asset, not the negotiator. Her handler from those days, Marek, denies everything too smoothly. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering your memory has been curated.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback-structured chapter following the night of the original 'favor': young Quentin talked a dying man off a bridge because someone on comms told her exactly what to say. Present-day Marek offers protection if she stays quiet. POV: alternating Quentin/Marek. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as leash.

chapters.title: The Stranger Returns
chapters.summary: The stranger, Ilse Brandt, surfaces—a former program colleague turned whistleblower target—and tells Quentin the network plans to use her voice to talk Ilse into silence before Frankfurt opens. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: recognition between two ghosts; reluctant alliance formed over bad coffee.

chapters.title: Collateral Skills
chapters.summary: The network tests Quentin's obedience by making her negotiate a staged crisis that goes live when she hesitates; a bystander dies. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose—the price of survival just got itemized.

chapters.title: Markets Open in Nine Hours
chapters.summary: Quentin plays along, feeding her handlers a script while secretly copying the program's ledger of manufactured negotiators. Marek suspects; he assigns a watcher she once trained. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: cold clarity—she is best when lying to professionals.

chapters.title: The Room Where Voices Are Made
chapters.summary: Quentin infiltrates the program's Frankfurt safehouse and finds the archive: recordings of every 'favor,' including her own. The watcher catches her but chooses, ambiguously, not to report. POV: watcher (Dane). Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth splits down the middle of a single person.

chapters.title: Negotiating With Ghosts
chapters.summary: Cornered, Quentin does what she does best: she talks. Facing Marek across a table, she trades the ledger's location for Ilse's safety, knowing he'll double-cross. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the climax of craft—every rule she learned weaponized against its authors.

chapters.title: Burn Before Opening
chapters.summary: As Frankfurt markets open, Quentin broadcasts the ledger to regulators and press while Marek's team closes in; Dane holds the door, paying his own debt. Marek falls; the network fractures publicly. POV: Quentin/Dane. Emotional beat: catharsis with shrapnel in it.

chapters.title: Named Witness
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Quentin testifies under her real name, visits the family of the man from her original failure, and finally answers a ringing phone without a script. Ilse sends no envelope—just a postcard. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned; invisibility surrendered willingly.
